title: The struck-down obscenity provision that's still being misused
p1: A law can disappear from the books… but still live on in people’s minds. That’s exactly what happened with a controversial online speech provision that many still wrongly believe can be used today.
p2: Many people don’t know that Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015. The Court found that its vague wording could restrict free speech. Yet, complaints and threats under this dead provision have continued to surface.
p3: The lesson is simple: a police complaint or legal notice does not automatically mean a law is valid. Citizens, businesses, and online users should check whether the provision being cited actually exists and can legally be enforced. Knowing this can prevent unnecessary fear and confusion when dealing with online expression issues.
conclusion: Have you ever seen someone threatened with a law that may no longer be valid? Should there be more awareness about outdated laws being used against people?
